description: An integer code present on almost all FDR events (236/275) that appears to identify which internal sensor subsystem, code path, or collection mechanism generated the event. No decode table or CIM mapping is available for it, so the specific meaning of each value cannot be confirmed from this KB.
hunting_notes: Because it rides on nearly every event, some hunters treat it as a coarse provenance/quality signal (e.g. distinguishing kernel-mode vs user-mode or ETW vs driver-sourced telemetry) but no authoritative mapping is available here, so do not build detection logic on specific values without confirming them against CrowdStrike's own schema docs.
evidence: Name convention only ('origin' suggests provenance/source). type=integer, present on 236 of 275 events with no common co-occurring fields beyond the universal envelope, decode_field=None, no rows in cim/decode_tables.csv, cim_reachable=False. No documentation source on disk defines its value space.

description: The NetBIOS/hostname of the endpoint the sensor is running on (or, on cloud-asset events such as AwsEc2Instance/AzureVirtualMachine, the reported instance name). Distinct from 'aid', which is CrowdStrike's opaque agent ID.
hunting_notes: Primary human-readable host identifier for pivoting and reporting; use alongside 'aid' since hostnames can be reused/renamed while aid is stable. Also appears on cloud inventory events (Azure/AWS/GCP), where it may reflect the cloud resource's configured name rather than an OS hostname.

join_candidates.why: aid is the stable per-sensor identifier for the same host that ComputerName names in human-readable form
ClientComputerName names a remote/client host in auth and SMB/WMI events; joining lets you resolve both sides of a cross-host interaction to hostnames

evidence: Name convention is unambiguous; appears on 57 varied events including host-identity events (AgentOnline with BiosManufacturer/SystemManufacturer/SystemProductName) and cloud asset events, consistent with a hostname field. type field was blank in fields.json (likely keyword/text), cim_reachable=False.

description: An internal sensor-assigned identifier for a specific file object, used to correlate multiple FDR records (e.g. FileCategory, Size, TargetFileName) that describe the same file-write event. It is not a content hash — separate SHA1/SHA256/MD5 fields exist for that.
hunting_notes: Useful for stitching together same-file records within a single file-write pipeline, but do not confuse it with a hash for cross-host or cross-time file identity matching — SHA256HashData/TargetFileName are the fields for that.
evidence: type=keyword, appears on 50 events, all in the *FileWritten family (AppleScriptFileWritten, AsifFileWritten, BZip2FileWritten, ...); co-occurs consistently with FileCategory, Size, TargetFileName, IsOnRemovableDisk. Intersection across all 50 events is just ['EventOrigin'], confirming it's scoped to the file-write event family rather than a general envelope field.

description: The account name (not SID) of the user associated with the event — e.g. the logged-on user for a process, file write, or logon/logoff event.
hunting_notes: High-value pivot field for 'what did this user do' hunts; note the Splunk TA's own EVAL logic falls back to UserPrincipal when UserName is empty on UserLogon, implying UserName can be blank/unreliable on some platforms — pair with UserPrincipal and UserSid for robustness.

join_candidates.why: same logical user, SID form; SID is stable across renames and works cross-locale
UPN form of the same user identity, used by the TA as a fallback for UserName
logon events pair UserName with RemoteAccount to distinguish local vs. remote-originated account context

evidence: cim_reachable=True with multiple EVAL mappings (user, user_name, src_user_name, object) driven by event_simpleName across UserLogon/UserLogoff/ProcessRollup2/etc; appears on 94 events; name is unambiguous and corroborated by CIM's own field name choice ('user').

description: An enum classifying the type/format of a file that was written to disk (the *FileWritten event family: BmpFileWritten, CabFileWritten, DmgFileWritten, PdfFileWritten, etc.), likely holding a value like the literal file type name or a corresponding code.
hunting_notes: Lets a hunter filter file-write telemetry by file type class without enumerating every *FileWritten event_simpleName individually; useful for spotting anomalous categories (e.g. executable-category writes to unusual paths).

join_candidates.why: both scoped to the same *FileWritten event family and same file instance

evidence: type=keyword, 37 events, all *FileWritten types; intersection across all its events = ['EventOrigin','FileIdentifier','IsOnRemovableDisk','Size','TargetFileName'], i.e. it always travels with the core file-write field set. No decode table entry found under this exact name in cim/decode_tables.csv, so exact enum values are unconfirmed.

description: A container/object field grouping ATT&CK-style attack metadata (its children Attacks.Tactic and Attacks.Technique) attached to file-write and other detection-adjacent events.
hunting_notes: Treat as the parent object for Attacks.Tactic/Attacks.Technique; querying tools that don't flatten nested objects may need to reference the child fields directly instead of this parent.
evidence: type field blank in fields.json (consistent with a nested/object container); 29 events, and its intersection-with-itself co-occurrence is exactly its two children ['Attacks.Tactic','Attacks.Technique'], confirming a parent/child nested relationship.

description: The MITRE ATT&CK tactic name (e.g. 'Defense Evasion', 'Execution') associated with a file-write or detection event, mirroring the top-level Tactic/MitreAttack.Tactic fields used elsewhere in the schema.
hunting_notes: Directly usable for ATT&CK-based hunting/coverage mapping; because the same concept appears under three different field names in this schema (Attacks.Tactic, Tactic, MitreAttack.Tactic depending on event type), normalize across all three before building a single ATT&CK dashboard.

join_candidates.why: same MITRE ATT&CK tactic vocabulary, used on a different event family (detection summary events)
sibling field on the same nested Attacks object, technique detail for this tactic

evidence: Name convention (ATT&CK 'Tactic' terminology) corroborated by an identical top-level 'Tactic' field used on cloud detection-summary events and by 'MitreAttack.Tactic' on others — three parallel spellings of the same concept across the schema is strong corroboration despite no direct decode table.

description: The MITRE ATT&CK technique name/ID associated with a file-write or detection event, sibling to Attacks.Tactic.
data_format: UTF-8 string (ATT&CK technique name or ID)
hunting_notes: Pair with Attacks.Tactic for full ATT&CK context; same normalization caveat as Attacks.Tactic applies (Technique / MitreAttack.Technique are parallel fields elsewhere).

join_candidates.why: same MITRE ATT&CK technique vocabulary, used on the cloud detection-summary event family
sibling field on the same nested Attacks object

evidence: Same basis as Attacks.Tactic: consistent naming pattern against 'Technique' and 'MitreAttack.Technique' elsewhere in the schema, and always co-occurs with Attacks.Tactic on the same 29 events.

description: A raw Windows kernel FILE_OBJECT pointer/handle used by the filesystem minifilter driver to correlate related IRP-level events for the same open file instance (e.g. DirectoryCreate, FsPostOpenSnapshotFile).
hunting_notes: Only meaningful for correlating events within a single session on a single host — kernel object addresses are not stable across reboots or hosts, so never join across aid/time boundaries on this field alone.
evidence: type=keyword, 21 events, always co-occurring with MajorFunction, MinorFunction, IrpFlags, OperationFlags — the classic Windows I/O Request Packet (IRP) field set used by filesystem minifilter drivers, which strongly corroborates 'FileObject' as the Windows kernel FILE_OBJECT term.

description: The Windows IRP (I/O Request Packet) major function code identifying the type of filesystem operation (e.g. IRP_MJ_CREATE, IRP_MJ_WRITE) captured by the minifilter driver.
hunting_notes: Standard Windows kernel constant; useful to filter minifilter telemetry down to specific operation types (e.g. only creates) across DirectoryCreate/FsPostOpenSnapshotFile/FileOpenInfo-style events.

join_candidates.why: IRP major/minor function codes are always interpreted together per Windows I/O manager convention

evidence: type=keyword, 21 events, always co-occurring with MinorFunction, FileObject, IrpFlags, OperationFlags — this is the standard Windows Filter Manager/IRP field set; name matches the well-known IRP_MJ_* constant family exactly.

description: The Windows IRP minor function code, refining MajorFunction with a more specific sub-operation (e.g. IRP_MN_NORMAL) for the same filesystem minifilter callback.
hunting_notes: Always interpret alongside MajorFunction; rarely useful alone.

join_candidates.why: IRP major/minor function codes are always interpreted together

evidence: Same event set and co-occurrence pattern as MajorFunction (21 events, filesystem minifilter family); name matches the standard Windows IRP_MN_* terminology.

description: The Windows access-rights bitmask requested when opening a handle to a file or process (the DesiredAccess parameter of NtCreateFile/NtOpenProcess), e.g. GENERIC_READ, PROCESS_VM_READ.
hunting_notes: Central to handle-access hunting — e.g. LSASS handle opens requesting PROCESS_VM_READ/PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS are a credential-dumping indicator; this field appears specifically on the *HandleOpDetectInfo/*FromUnsignedModule events built for that purpose.
evidence: type=keyword, 12 events including LsassHandleFromUnsignedModule, FalconProcessHandleOpDetectInfo, PrivilegedProcessHandleFromUnsignedModule (all handle-access detections) and file-open events (DirectoryCreate, FileOpenInfo) — exactly the contexts where Windows DesiredAccess is captured.

description: The MS-RPC operation number (opnum) identifying which remote procedure was invoked on the RPC interface named by InterfaceGuid/InterfaceVersion.
hunting_notes: Useful for spotting known-malicious RPC opnums against sensitive interfaces (e.g. DCSync-style directory-replication calls, service-control or scheduled-task RPC abuse) once mapped to the interface's IDL — requires an external opnum-to-method table since no decode is present here.

join_candidates.why: an opnum is only meaningful in the context of the RPC interface it belongs to

evidence: type=keyword, 12 events (BITSJobCreated, HostedServiceStarted, ScheduledTaskRegistered/Modified/Deleted, ServiceStarted, UserAccountAddedToGroup, NetShareSecurityModify) all co-occurring with InterfaceGuid, InterfaceVersion, RpcNestingLevel, RpcClientProcessId/ThreadId — the standard MS-RPC call-context field set.

description: Paired with BoundingLimitCount, likely the time-window (duration) over which the sensor caps/throttles how many instances of a given event or detection it will emit, to prevent event floods.
data_format: keyword (numeric, unit unconfirmed — possibly seconds or ms)
hunting_notes: If present with a low BoundingLimitCount, indicates the underlying event stream was rate-limited during that window — a hunter relying on raw counts from these event types (DetectionExcluded, FileWrittenWithEntropyHigh, RansomwareOpenFile) should check this pair before treating volume as ground truth.

join_candidates.why: the two fields always co-occur and together define a rate-limit window (count per duration)

evidence: type=keyword, 11 events, intersection across all of them = ['BoundingLimitCount','EventOrigin'] — always paired with BoundingLimitCount specifically, on events known to be rate/volume-sensitive (RansomwareOpenFile, FileWrittenWithEntropyHigh, DetectionExcluded). Exact units not confirmed by any decode table.

description: A field on network connection events (NetworkConnectIP4/6, NetworkCloseIP4/6, NetworkListenIP4/6, etc.) whose exact meaning is unclear; the name suggests it flags whether the connection was captured with full process/thread context attached versus observed out-of-band.
hunting_notes: If it does mark process-context completeness, connections with InContext=false (or equivalent) may be worth extra scrutiny since they'd lack reliable process attribution via ContextProcessId — but this interpretation is not confirmed by any decode table.
evidence: type=keyword, 11 events, all network connection lifecycle events, always co-occurring with ConnectionDirection, ConnectionFlags, LocalPort, Protocol, RemotePort. No decode table entry and no CIM mapping found, so this is a name-convention guess only.

description: A bitmask capturing Windows filter-manager 'Extra Create Parameters' (ECP) flags present on the file-create IRP — additional create-time context such as transactional or reparse-related parameters.
hunting_notes: The Splunk TA references a bitmask lookup table for this field (crowdstrike_ta_bitmask_lookup_FileEcpBitmask) that is not present in this KB's decode_tables.csv, so bit-level meaning can't be resolved here — treat individual bit values as unknown until that lookup is sourced.
evidence: cim_reachable=True via a LOOKUP-type CIM mapping ('FileEcpBitmask_meaning' from crowdstrike_ta_bitmask_lookup_FileEcpBitmask), confirming it is a decodable bitmask in CrowdStrike's own TA, though the actual lookup values aren't present in cim/decode_tables.csv. Appears on 19 filesystem minifilter events (DirectoryCreate, DmpFileWritten, FsPostOpenSnapshotFile, ...) alongside FileObject/MajorFunction/MinorFunction.

description: The Windows network interface index (ifIndex) of the network adapter involved in the event — the standard integer handle used by Windows networking APIs to identify a NIC.
hunting_notes: Useful to correlate a DNS request or interface-state event to a specific physical/virtual adapter on the host, especially on multi-homed hosts (VPN adapters, VMs, etc.).

join_candidates.why: both identify the same network adapter via different Windows networking identifier schemes and co-occur on the same LocalIpAddress* events

evidence: type=long, appears on DnsRequest, LocalIpAddressIP4/IP6, LocalIpAddressRemovedIP4/IP6, NeighborListIP4/IP6, SuspiciousDnsRequest — all networking/adapter-state events, alongside InterfaceAlias/InterfaceType/PhysicalAddress, matching the standard Windows adapter-enumeration field set.

description: An internal CrowdStrike index/code classifying the type or sensitivity of a registry key/value being modified, paired with RegClassification and RegClassificationFlags.
hunting_notes: Likely usable to filter registry telemetry to specific classes of interest (e.g. autostart/ASEP-relevant keys) without string-matching RegObjectName, but the index-to-meaning mapping is not present in this KB.

join_candidates.why: co-occurs identically across all 6 registry-update events and is presumably the numeric form of the same classification RegClassification names

evidence: type=keyword, 6 events (AsepValueUpdate-adjacent RegCrowdstrikeValueUpdate, RegGenericKeyUpdate, RegGenericValueUpdate, RegSystemConfigKeyUpdate/ValueUpdate, RegistryOperationDetectInfo), always co-occurring with RegClassification/RegClassificationFlags/RegObjectName. No decode table entry found under this name.

description: The name of the registry value that was created, modified, or deleted (the value-name component of a registry path, as opposed to the key path itself).
hunting_notes: Combine with RegObjectName (key path) and RegStringValue/RegType to reconstruct the full registry change; classic autostart/persistence hunting field (e.g. spotting new Run-key values).

join_candidates.why: RegObjectName is the key path; RegValueName is the value within it — together they form the full registry location

evidence: type=keyword, 6 registry-update events, always co-occurring with RegObjectName, RegType, RegStringValue — standard Windows registry terminology and structure.

description: The Windows file-sharing mode flags (FILE_SHARE_READ/WRITE/DELETE) requested when a file handle was opened, alongside DesiredAccess.
hunting_notes: Useful to spot unusual open modes (e.g. a process opening another process's file with no sharing allowed, blocking legitimate access) in file-open telemetry.

join_candidates.why: both are parameters of the same NtCreateFile-style open call captured on the same events

evidence: type=keyword, 6 events (DirectoryCreate, FileOpenInfo, FsPostOpenSnapshotFile, NewExecutableWritten, NewScriptWritten, RansomwareOpenFile), always co-occurring with DesiredAccess and Status — the standard Windows file-open parameter set.

description: A free-form tag/label list whose specific meaning varies by event: sensor grouping tags on CurrentSystemTags, detection tags on Event_DetectionSummaryEvent, and upload-context tags on LfoUpload*/ProcessRollup2/RansomwareFileAccessPattern.
hunting_notes: Because the field is reused across unrelated event families with different content, do not assume a single vocabulary — check event_simpleName before interpreting a Tags value.
evidence: type=keyword, 6 events spanning unrelated families (CurrentSystemTags, Event_DetectionSummaryEvent, LfoUploadDataComplete/Start, ProcessRollup2, RansomwareFileAccessPattern) with no shared co-occurring fields beyond envelope — the field name is generic and the contexts are too heterogeneous to pin down one meaning confidently.

description: An epoch timestamp (distinct from the envelope's 'timestamp' and 'ContextTimeStamp') present on cloud-generated detection/lead summary events, likely marking when the underlying detection/signal occurred as reported by the cloud analytics pipeline.
hunting_notes: On detection-summary events this may be the most reliable 'when did this really happen' field if it differs from ingestion-time 'timestamp' — worth comparing the two to detect backfill/delay in the detection pipeline.
evidence: Appears only on Event_AutomatedLeadSummaryEvent, Event_DataProtectionDetectionSummaryEvent, Event_DetectionSummaryEvent, Event_EppDetectionSummaryEvent, Event_FileIntegrityMonitorRuleMatchedEnriched — all cloud-side 'Event_*' detection/summary types (distinct from raw sensor telemetry), which is why it exists alongside but separately from the envelope 'timestamp'. Field type was blank in fields.json.

description: A string-form customer/tenant identifier on cloud-generated detection summary events, likely a longer or differently-formatted representation of the tenant than the short envelope 'cid'.
hunting_notes: Use for tenant scoping on Event_*SummaryEvent records specifically; verify it matches 'cid' if cross-referencing with raw sensor telemetry for the same tenant.

join_candidates.why: both identify the customer/tenant; CustomerIdString is the string form used on cloud summary events while cid is the short form on raw telemetry

evidence: Appears only on the 5 Event_*SummaryEvent types, always alongside 'cid' in the same records (per envelope), and the name directly parallels 'cid' (customer id).

description: The IO_STATUS_BLOCK.Information value returned by the Windows I/O manager on a file-create/open operation, indicating the operation's disposition (e.g. FILE_CREATED, FILE_OPENED, FILE_OVERWRITTEN, FILE_SUPERSEDED).
hunting_notes: Distinguishes 'file already existed and was opened' from 'file was newly created' from 'file was overwritten' — useful to separate genuine new-file-write detections from routine opens of pre-existing files.
evidence: type=keyword, 5 filesystem minifilter events (DirectoryCreate, FsPostOpenSnapshotFile, NewExecutableWritten, NewScriptWritten, RansomwareOpenFile), always co-occurring with Status, MajorFunction, MinorFunction, IrpFlags — exactly the IRP-completion field set where Windows' IO_STATUS_BLOCK.Information lives.

description: An unsigned integer present on cloud-generated detection/lead summary events, likely a dedup/idempotency token or correlation nonce generated by the cloud pipeline rather than the sensor.
evidence: type=unsigned_long, appears only on the 5 Event_*SummaryEvent cloud detection types. The name is a standard cryptographic/idempotency term but no decode table, CIM mapping, or further context confirms its exact role here.

description: The macOS Open Directory node name (e.g. '/Local/Default') on which a directory-service operation (attribute add/remove/set, user creation, password modification) occurred.
hunting_notes: Useful for macOS local-account and directory-service hunting — pairs with ODRecordName/ODRecordType/ODAttributeName to fully describe the directory-service change.
evidence: type=keyword, 5 events, all OpenDirectory* (macOS-specific) events, always co-occurring with ODAttributeName, ODDatabasePath, ODErrorCode, ODRecordName/ODRecordType — unambiguous macOS Open Directory terminology.

description: The Windows CreateOptions flags passed to NtCreateFile (e.g. FILE_DIRECTORY_FILE, FILE_NON_DIRECTORY_FILE, FILE_SEQUENTIAL_ONLY) on a file-create/open operation.
hunting_notes: Combine with DesiredAccess/ShareAccess/Information for a full picture of how a file was opened.

join_candidates.why: both are parameters of the same NtCreateFile call captured on the same filesystem minifilter events

evidence: type=keyword, 5 filesystem minifilter events, always co-occurring with DesiredAccess, ShareAccess, FileAttributes, Information — the standard NtCreateFile parameter set.

description: The full command line of the parent process of the process associated with the event (typically a detection).
hunting_notes: Core process-lineage hunting field — inspect alongside CommandLine and GrandparentCommandLine to reconstruct a process ancestry chain for suspicious executions.

join_candidates.why: same process-lineage record; ParentCommandLine describes the direct parent of the process CommandLine describes
extends the same ancestry chain one level further up
ParentProcessId is the numeric identity of the same parent process this field's command line belongs to

evidence: Appears on Event_DetectionSummaryEvent/Event_EppDetectionSummaryEvent and FalconProcessHandleOpDetectInfo always alongside GrandparentCommandLine/GrandparentImageFileName and ParentProcessId — standard process-ancestry field naming used throughout the schema.

description: The memory address at which an injected/created thread began execution, captured by thread-injection detection telemetry.
hunting_notes: Classic code-injection hunting field — an unusual start address (not aligned to a loaded module's code section) is a strong indicator of shellcode/reflective injection; compare against loaded-module ranges for the target process.

join_candidates.why: sibling field capturing the equivalent start address in the source/injecting process's context

evidence: type=keyword, 5 events, all in the injected-thread family (BrowserInjectedThread, DllInjection, DocumentProgramInjectedThread, InjectedThread, JavaInjectedThread), always co-occurring with SourceThreadStartAddress, ThreadStartContext, RawThreadId/TargetThreadId, UserThread.

description: A value accompanying ThreadStartAddress on injected-thread events; likely either a pointer to the thread's initial CONTEXT/register state or a classification code describing how the thread's start was constructed. The exact interpretation is not confirmed.
hunting_notes: Analyze together with ThreadStartAddress and InjectedThreadFlag when triaging injection detections; treat as supplementary context rather than a primary indicator until its exact semantics are confirmed.
evidence: type=keyword, same 5 injected-thread events as ThreadStartAddress, always co-occurring with it. No decode table or CIM mapping found, and the name is ambiguous between 'context record' and 'context classification' readings.

description: A short integer field on cloud-generated Event_*SummaryEvent records, alongside 'cid'; likely a numeric event/schema identifier for the summary-event type, distinct from the sensor-side event_simpleName/id fields.
evidence: type=integer, appears only on the 5 Event_*SummaryEvent cloud detection types, always paired with 'cid' rather than the usual raw-telemetry envelope (aid/id/name/event_platform are absent on these events). No decode table or documentation confirms the exact meaning.

description: The full registry object path (hive plus key path) that a registry operation targeted; CrowdStrike's own CIM mapping splits it into registry_hive, registry_path, and registry_value_name.
hunting_notes: Primary field for registry-based persistence/tamper hunting; the CIM split into hive/path/value_name shows this is a composite path string that a hunter may want to parse similarly.

join_candidates.why: RegObjectName is the key path context that RegValueName's value name lives under

evidence: cim_reachable=True with cim_fields=['registry_hive','registry_path','registry_value_name'], confirming it is CIM-normalized as the composite registry path; appears on 9 registry-operation events (AsepKeyUpdate, AsepValueUpdate, RegGenericKeyUpdate/ValueUpdate, RegistryOperationDetectInfo, SuspiciousRegAsepUpdate, ...).

description: The hostname of the remote/client machine involved in a network logon, SMB share access, or WMI/DCSync-style directory-service operation — distinct from ComputerName, which names the local host running the sensor.
hunting_notes: Useful for lateral-movement hunting (e.g. which remote host initiated a logon or SMB session against this endpoint); CIM maps it to dest_name/object/src depending on event, so the 'direction' (source vs destination) is event-specific — verify against event_simpleName before assuming src vs. dst semantics.

join_candidates.why: if the remote host is also monitored, its own ComputerName record can be joined to enrich ClientComputerName with that host's other telemetry

evidence: cim_reachable=True (dest_name/object/src), 8 events (DCSyncAttempted, ProcessExecOnSMBFile, SensitiveWmiQuery, SmbClientShareClosedEtw/OpenedEtw, UserLogon, UserLogonFailed2, WmiProviderRegistrationEtw) — all remote-interaction event types, consistent with a remote/client host name.

description: An identifier tying together the set of USB descriptor sub-events (configuration, endpoint, HID, interface) that belong to the same physical USB device enumeration, alongside DeviceDescriptorSetHash.
hunting_notes: Use to reassemble the full USB descriptor set for a single device-connect event across the DcUsb* event family rather than relying on timestamp proximity alone.

join_candidates.why: both scope to the same USB descriptor set and co-occur on all four DcUsb* descriptor events

evidence: type=keyword, 4 events, all DcUsb*Descriptor events (DcUsbConfigurationDescriptor, DcUsbEndpointDescriptor, DcUsbHIDDescriptor, DcUsbInterfaceDescriptor), always co-occurring with DeviceDescriptorSetHash and DeviceTimeStamp.

description: The X.509 Extended Key Usage (EKU) OIDs from the code-signing certificate of a module/file involved in an unsigned-module or handle-access detection.
hunting_notes: Legitimate code-signing certs typically carry the 'Code Signing' EKU; unexpected or missing EKUs on a signing cert attached to a sensitive-handle-open event is a useful triage signal.

join_candidates.why: ExtendedKeyUsages is an attribute of the same signing certificate captured in the Certificate field

evidence: type=keyword, 4 events (LsassHandleFromUnsignedModule, PrivilegedProcessHandleFromUnsignedModule, SAMHashDumpFromUnsignedModule, UnsignedModuleLoad), always co-occurring with Certificate, PublicKeys, SignInfoFlags — standard PKI/code-signing terminology and context.

description: A URL linking directly to the corresponding detection's page in the Falcon console (the product's former name, 'Falcon Host').
hunting_notes: Handy for auto-generating pivot links from a SIEM/SOAR alert straight into the Falcon UI for analyst triage.
evidence: type=keyword, 4 events, all cloud detection-summary types (Event_AutomatedLeadSummaryEvent, Event_DataProtectionDetectionSummaryEvent, Event_DetectionSummaryEvent, Event_EppDetectionSummaryEvent); name directly references the 'Falcon Host' product and a console link is a standard feature of CrowdStrike's detection-summary webhooks.

description: A field on network-adapter state events (LocalIpAddressIP4/IP6 and their Removed variants) whose name suggests it identifies which OS telemetry pipeline or API (e.g. WMI, netlink, ETW) supplied the adapter data. Exact semantics are unconfirmed.
evidence: type=keyword, 4 events (LocalIpAddressIP4, LocalIpAddressIP6, LocalIpAddressRemovedIP4, LocalIpAddressRemovedIP6), always co-occurring with InterfaceIndex/NetLuidIndex. No decode table or CIM mapping found; 'pipeline source' is a plausible but unconfirmed reading of the name.

description: The Windows NET_LUID index of the network interface — a locally-unique identifier Windows assigns to each network adapter instance, alongside the more familiar InterfaceIndex.
hunting_notes: Use interchangeably with InterfaceIndex to pin an event to a specific adapter; NET_LUID is the newer Windows identifier scheme and may be more stable across adapter renumbering than ifIndex.

join_candidates.why: both identify the same network adapter via parallel Windows identifier schemes and co-occur on the same LocalIpAddress* events

evidence: type=long, 4 events (LocalIpAddressIP4/IP6, LocalIpAddressRemovedIP4/IP6), always co-occurring with InterfaceIndex — 'NET_LUID' is a standard, unambiguous Windows networking API term.

description: The timestamp of when the authenticating user's password was last changed, captured on logon/logoff and user-identity events.
data_format: keyword (likely epoch or Windows FILETIME string, unconfirmed exact encoding)
hunting_notes: Useful for spotting logons using very old (or suspiciously never-changed) passwords, and for correlating with password-spray/credential-stuffing hunts.

join_candidates.why: attribute of the same authenticating user identity captured alongside it on UserLogon/UserLogoff/UserIdentity

evidence: type=keyword, 4 events (UserIdentity, UserLogoff, UserLogon, UserLogonFailed), always co-occurring with LogonTime/LogonType/UserSid/UserName — standard Windows authentication field naming, though exact timestamp encoding is not confirmed by a conversions entry.

description: The public key(s) extracted from the code-signing certificate of a module/file involved in an unsigned-module or sensitive-handle detection.
hunting_notes: Can be used to cluster files signed by the same key/certificate even when the certificate's display fields differ, useful for tracking a threat actor's signing infrastructure.

join_candidates.why: PublicKeys is extracted from the same signing certificate captured in the Certificate field

evidence: type=keyword, 4 events (LsassHandleFromUnsignedModule, PrivilegedProcessHandleFromUnsignedModule, SAMHashDumpFromUnsignedModule, UnsignedModuleLoad), always co-occurring with Certificate, ExtendedKeyUsages, SignInfoFlags.

description: A field on logon/logoff and user-identity events whose name suggests it flags or names an account associated with a remote (network) logon, as opposed to an interactive local logon.
data_format: keyword (unconfirmed — could be boolean-like or a name)
hunting_notes: If it does flag remote-originated accounts, it's a useful complement to LogonType for distinguishing network logons (Type 3) from interactive ones — but this reading is unconfirmed.

join_candidates.why: co-occurs on the same logon/logoff/identity events and likely refers to the same or a related account context

evidence: type=keyword, 4 events (LogonBehaviorCompositionDetectInfo, UserIdentity, UserLogoff, UserLogon), always co-occurring with LogonDomain/LogonType/UserName/UserSid. No decode table entry found under this name, so the exact value space (boolean flag vs. account name) is not confirmed.

description: The human-readable display name of a Windows service (as shown in the Services MMC snap-in), distinct from the service's internal short name.
hunting_notes: Useful for spotting services impersonating legitimate-sounding display names while having suspicious ImagePath/binary; combine with ServiceImagePath-style fields (ModifyServiceBinary's ServiceImagePath) for full context.
evidence: cim_reachable=True (service, service_name), 8 events (DriverLoad, HostedServiceStarted/Stopped, KernelServiceStarted, ModifyServiceBinary, ServiceStarted/Stopped, ServicesStatusInfo) — standard Windows Service Control Manager terminology.

description: The start address of the thread in the source/injecting process's context, paired with ThreadStartAddress which captures the equivalent address in the target process, on thread-injection detection events.
hunting_notes: Compare against ThreadStartAddress and the source process's loaded-module ranges to determine whether the injection originated from legitimate code or from an unbacked/suspicious region.

join_candidates.why: sibling field on the same injected-thread events; together they describe both sides (source and target) of the injection

evidence: type=keyword, 4 events (BrowserInjectedThread, DocumentProgramInjectedThread, InjectedThread, JavaInjectedThread), always co-occurring with ThreadStartAddress/ThreadStartContext/UserThread. 'Source' naming convention strongly implies a source-vs-target pairing but the exact process-side semantics aren't documented on disk.

description: A field on thread-injection detection events (BrowserInjectedThread, DocumentProgramInjectedThread, InjectedThread, JavaInjectedThread) whose name suggests it flags whether the target thread is a user-mode thread, or otherwise characterizes the thread's execution context.

join_candidates.why: co-occurs as an attribute of the same target thread identified by TargetThreadId on injection events

evidence: type=keyword, 4 events, always co-occurring with ThreadStartAddress/ThreadStartContext/SourceThreadStartAddress/RawThreadId/TargetThreadId. No decode table or CIM mapping found; name is ambiguous.

description: The drive letter (e.g. 'D:') assigned to a volume when it is mounted, on volume-mount and removable-media events.
hunting_notes: Direct hunting value for removable-media and volume-mount monitoring (e.g. correlating a new drive letter with a subsequent burst of file-write activity on that same letter).
evidence: type=keyword, 4 events (FsVolumeMounted, MountedVolume, RemovableMediaVolumeMounted, VolumeSnapshotDeleted), co-occurring with VolumeFileSystemDevice/Driver, VolumeMountPoint, VolumeName — standard Windows storage-stack field family; name is unambiguous.

description: The name of the underlying file-system device object for a mounted volume (e.g. a \Device\HarddiskVolumeN-style path).
hunting_notes: Useful to correlate a drive letter/mount point back to the physical/virtual device backing it, e.g. distinguishing a real disk from a mounted image or virtual disk.

join_candidates.why: sibling field naming the driver that services this same device object

evidence: type=keyword, 4 events (FsVolumeMounted, MountedVolume, RemovableMediaVolumeMounted, SnapshotVolumeMounted), co-occurring with VolumeDriveLetter, VolumeFileSystemDriver, VolumeMountPoint — standard Windows storage-stack terminology.

description: The name of the file-system driver servicing a mounted volume (e.g. NTFS, FAT32, exFAT, ReFS).
hunting_notes: Lets a hunter flag unusual filesystem types on removable/mounted volumes (e.g. exFAT USB drives vs. expected NTFS internal volumes).

join_candidates.why: sibling field naming the device object this driver services

evidence: Same 4 volume-mount events as VolumeFileSystemDevice, always co-occurring with it and VolumeFileSystemType — standard Windows filesystem terminology.

description: Whether the mounted volume is encrypted (e.g. via BitLocker), on volume-mount events.
hunting_notes: Useful for data-loss-prevention hunting on removable media (e.g. flagging unencrypted removable volumes being mounted) and for encryption-compliance auditing.

join_candidates.why: co-occurs on the same events and likely carries the more detailed encryption state that this boolean summarizes

evidence: type=keyword but name and context (co-occurs with VolumeEncryptionStatus on MountedVolume/RemovableMediaVolumeMounted/SnapshotVolumeMounted) make the boolean semantics unambiguous despite the underlying ES field type being 'keyword' rather than 'boolean'.
